cues.label: Catch a falling rocket
cues.voice: This tower just caught a rocket. How does it avoid disaster?

cues.label: First, remove the speed
cues.voice: Coming home means killing speed. Fire too late, and even full thrust cannot save the landing.

cues.label: Steer through the air
cues.voice: These grid fins bite into the air. Sensors track every movement, and the computer keeps correcting the path.

cues.label: Point the thrust
cues.voice: Near the ground, the engine tilts. Its thrust pushes the booster sideways as the landing burn bleeds off speed.

cues.label: Four legs. One landing.
cues.voice: Falcon Nine unfolds four legs. The engine does the braking. Only after touchdown do the legs carry the rocket.

cues.label: The tower takes the load
cues.voice: Super Heavy takes a different route. The tower supports two dedicated catch points, not the grid fins. The engines shut down. The tower takes the weight.

cues.label: Try changing the timing
cues.voice: A little more wind. A later ignition. Suddenly, that perfect return becomes a missed landing. Can you get the timing right?

cues.label: Your turn to land it
cues.voice: Land it yourself. Try the interactive lab at How Things Click dot com.
